newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka says 214 rebels killed in offensive.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka says 214 rebels killed in offensive.

text.p: Sri Lanka said on Saturday that 214 Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) rebels had been killed in the latest offensive in the north.
The defence ministry said in a statement that the LTTE's radio had announced a list of 214 dead and said that 310 rebels had been wounded in fighting in the northern Wanni region.
But LTTE's international spokesman in London denied so many rebels had died, saying the government usually exaggerated their casualties.
"I am disputing the figure. The defence ministry's figures are a fabrication. They always exaggerate LTTE casualties. We have lost only 72 people," Anton Rajah told Reuters.

The defence ministry statement added that troops were consolidating their positions in the newly captured areas north of Omanthai and Nedunkeni, which the military took from the rebels after fighting in the past two weeks.
It said there were minor clashes between the troops in the forward defence line and the rebels on Saturday and that the LTTE suffered some casualties.

Two army divisions, consisting of some 20,000 troops, launched "Operation Jaya Sikuru", or "Sure of Victory", from Vavuniya 220 km (135 miles) north of Colombo, on May 13 in a bid to open a supply route to the Jaffna peninsula, 100 km (60 miles) further north.
Soldiers captured Omanthai and Rambaikulam, 17 km (10 miles) north of the government-controlled northern frontline town of Vavuniya, after launching a two-pronged thrust into the Wanni region.
The other flank was opened by the army from the northeastern Weli Oya when they captured Nedunkeni, some 40 km (25 miles) northeast of Vavuniya.

The LTTE are fighting a 13-year-old war for an independent homeland for minority Tamils in mainly Sinhalese Sri Lanka's north and east. The government says more than 50,000 people have been killed in the war. The rebels say the toll is higher.
